interpretation: As part of the weekly reset, walk every point of use (each bathroom's toilet-paper holder and spare-roll basket, tissue boxes, hand-soap pumps, kitchen paper towels, dish soap, dishwasher pods, trash-liner rolls, laundry detergent) and bring each back to its household par level from the backstock shelf, using the oldest backstock first and adding anything whose backstock fell below the reorder point to the shared shopping list.
conditional: Point-of-use below par: refill from backstock with the matching product; already at par: leave it alone (do not open a new package or overfill); backstock for that item empty: add it to the shopping list and tell a resident instead of substituting a different product (e.g. never fill the hand-soap pump with dish soap).
success: Every tracked point-of-use location is at or above its par level with the correct product; backstock counts decreased by exactly what was moved (no items appear from nowhere); oldest backstock units were used first; items with backstock below reorder point are on the shopping list; no dispenser overflowed; empty cardboard cores are in recycling.
wrong: Refills the bathroom hand-soap pump with dish soap or a cleaner because the soap refill ran out
Restocks only the kitchen and skips the upstairs bathroom and powder room
Opens a fresh multipack and places it in front of the partially used one, or does not record the empty backstock on the shopping list
protect: guest-bath decorative towels or reserved items consumed
fidelity: S: per-location counts vs par, backstock conservation and reorder list; refill pour is a scalar volume with an overflow threshold
user_sim: Hidden: household par levels per location (e.g. 2 spare rolls per bathroom, 1 spare liner roll under kitchen sink) and preferred products. Unnecessary question: 'Which soap goes in the bathroom pump?' when the refill is labeled. Necessary communication: telling the resident that an item has no backstock (a report, not a question).
notes: Weekly reset section; same skill as the Restock primitive (P-8485e901f13699-01) and the per-item restock tasks in Kitchen/Bathrooms/Laundry (e.g. 'Restock toilet paper', 'Restock paper towels'). Scenario must randomize which locations are below par and which backstocks are empty.

interpretation: Weekly-reset pass over every mirror in the home: bathroom vanity mirrors (toothpaste spatter, water spots, hairspray film), the entry/hall mirror (fingerprints, smudges) and bedroom full-length mirrors (dust, kid handprints). Spray glass cleaner onto a microfiber cloth rather than at the mirror edge, wipe top to bottom including the top edge, and buff to streak-free.
success: Every mirror in the household registry has soil coverage below threshold and streak/lint score below threshold across the whole surface including the top band; no liquid pooled at the mirror edges or soaked into wooden frames; toiletries moved off the vanity are back in their original positions; the used cloth is in the laundry.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly at the mirror so it runs behind the edge and into the frame (desilvering/frame swelling)
Wipes with a dry paper towel or the dirty bathroom cloth, leaving lint and streaks
Cleans only the main bathroom mirror and skips the hall and bedroom mirrors, or only the reachable lower two-thirds
protect: toiletries knocked into the sink or toilet
cleaner overspray on wood vanity or wallpaper
entering an occupied bathroom or bedroom
fidelity: G: wipe-path coverage over each mirror plane including the top band reached from floor or stool; streak as residual cleaner film scalar
notes: Weekly reset section. Shares the glass.wipe skill with 'Clean windows' and bathroom 'Clean mirrors'-type tasks; the full-length mirror and upper band test reach. Privacy: occupied bathroom/bedroom must be skipped and revisited.

interpretation: Weekly disinfection of the house's high-touch points: interior and exterior door knobs/levers, light switches, faucet and toilet-flush handles, fridge/microwave/oven handles, cabinet pulls, stair rail, TV remotes and game controllers. Clean visible grime first, then apply a material-appropriate disinfectant and leave it wet for the labeled contact time, using separate cloths for bathroom and kitchen points and never spraying liquid into switches or electronics.
success: Every object in the touchpoint registry has germ_load below threshold reached with the required contact time satisfied and no visible grime; no liquid ingress into switches, remotes or controllers; no cloth that touched a toilet flush lever later touched a kitchen surface; finishes undamaged; remotes back where they were.
wrong: Wipes the toilet flush lever and then the fridge handle with the same cloth
Sprays disinfectant straight onto light switches and the TV remote (liquid ingress/short)
Wipes disinfectant off immediately, or only does the kitchen and skips bedroom door knobs, stair rail and switches
protect: bleach damage to brass or natural-stone finishes
fidelity: S: touchpoint registry with germ_load, contact-time timers and cloth contamination state
notes: Weekly reset section. Related to sick-day 'disinfect' tasks and the Disinfect primitive (P-35637d8bbbd60e-01); scenario randomizes which touchpoints were contaminated and which materials (brass knob, granite-adjacent faucet, electronics) appear.

interpretation: Sweep the outdoor entry areas, meaning the front porch and steps, the back-door landing and the garage side-door stoop: sweep leaves, grit and dirt away from the threshold into a pile, collect it into a dustpan for the yard-waste bin, brush cobwebs out of the door-frame corners, and shake the doormat out away from the door before putting it back squarely.
success: Debris on every registered entry zone (front porch and steps, back landing, side stoop) is below threshold; the swept material is in the yard-waste bin (not in the doorway, on the walkway, in a storm drain or a neighbor's yard); doormats are shaken and realigned; no debris tracked inside; doors closed in their initial state.
wrong: Sweeps debris across the threshold into the house through the open door
Sweeps the pile off the porch onto the front walk, the street gutter or the neighbor's side
Does only the front porch and ignores the back and side entries, or shakes the doormat inside the entry
protect: door left open so the dog gets out
indoor broom used outdoors and returned dirty
fidelity: G: broom coverage of porch/step geometry including step edges and corners; debris as particle piles with wet-leaf adhesion
notes: Weekly reset section. Shares the sweep.outdoor skill with 'Sweep patio', 'Sweep porch' and the Sweep primitive (P-40e813894482c8-01); wet-leaf weather variant must change technique.

interpretation: Monthly deep clean of the refrigerator compartment: move food to a cooler zone-by-zone, discard spoiled or expired items, take out shelves and crisper drawers and wash them in warm soapy water (letting cold glass shelves warm up first), wipe walls, ceiling, door bins and gasket folds with a mild baking-soda solution, dry everything, reinstall in the original slots and return food with raw meat on the bottom.
conditional: Item expired, moldy or spoiled: discard (food to compost/trash, rinsed container to recycling); in date, or a labeled/unclear item owned by someone else: keep and return it (ask the owner if it looks questionable). Food out of cold storage longer than the time limit must go in a cooler; a short session can stay out.
success: Soil below threshold on every shelf, drawer, wall, door bin and gasket fold; shelves and drawers reinstalled in their original slots; only expired/spoiled items discarded and their containers in the right streams; every kept item back inside with cumulative time-out below the food-safety limit; raw meat on the lowest shelf; no cracked glass; fridge interior back at or below 4 C with the door sealed.
wrong: Wipes only the visible front edges and leaves the crisper drawers and moldy gasket folds untouched
Pours hot water on a cold glass shelf (cracks it) or leaves food on the counter for hours
Throws away in-date items or a housemate's labeled leftovers and the sourdough starter, or returns raw chicken to the top shelf above produce
protect: food warmed past the safe limit
fridge left unplugged or door ajar
fidelity: S: per-zone soil states, food time-out timers and glass-shelf temperature delta for the crack rule; G only for shelf/drawer slot reinstallation
user_sim: Hidden: which questionable-looking items the owner wants kept (e.g. sourdough starter, aging cheese, 'Dad's - keep' leftovers). Necessary question: an unlabeled, ambiguous item that may belong to someone. Unnecessary question: whether to toss a visibly moldy item past its date.
notes: Monthly/occasional reset: deep version of Kitchen cleaning entries 'Clean refrigerator shelves/drawers/seals' and Food waste reduction 'Clean refrigerator spill'. Must not be passable by exterior wipe-down.

interpretation: Monthly freezer clean: move frozen items to a cooler with ice packs, discard freezer-burned or expired packages, remove built-up frost by defrosting (unplug or defrost mode, towels to catch meltwater, bowl of hot water; never chip ice with a knife), wipe shelves/bins and spills, dry fully, restart and return food in first-in-first-out order once the compartment is cold.
conditional: Frost thicker than the threshold: do a full defrost with meltwater management; thin frost: wipe without defrosting. Package freezer-burned/expired: discard; otherwise keep.
success: Frost below threshold, interior soil below threshold and dry; meltwater fully absorbed (no water on floor or in the fridge compartment); no punctured evaporator; all kept items still frozen when returned and ordered oldest in front; expired/freezer-burned items discarded; unit powered and back at or below -18 C.
wrong: Chips ice off with a knife or screwdriver, puncturing the evaporator/liner
Leaves food out on the counter until it thaws, then refreezes it
Lets meltwater flood the floor or the fridge section, or forgets to plug the freezer back in
fidelity: P: frost mass melting vs time and meltwater volume; food thaw state as a temperature integral
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning ('Clean freezer.', T-628f7de6f12425-01); here in the monthly-reset routine. Frost thickness and power-mode randomized.

interpretation: Monthly oven clean of baked-on grease and carbonized spills on the oven floor, walls, racks and door glass, starting only with a cold oven. Method depends on the oven: self-clean cycle with racks removed and the kitchen ventilated, or a baking-soda paste with overnight dwell, or caustic oven cleaner with gloves on a standard enamel oven only. Then wipe out the ash/residue, clean the racks and door glass, and reassemble.
conditional: Self-cleaning enamel: never use commercial caustic oven cleaner; run self-clean (racks out) only with approval, nobody away, kitchen ventilated, and NOT if a pet bird is in the home; otherwise use baking-soda paste. Standard (non-self-clean) oven: caustic cleaner allowed with gloves and ventilation, kept off the heating element and gasket.
success: Interior soil and door-glass soil below threshold; racks clean and back in place; no chemical residue left (pH-neutral wipe test); no enamel damage, gasket intact; if self-clean was used it was approved, racks were out, ventilation on, no bird exposure event; oven off and unlocked at end.
wrong: Sprays caustic oven cleaner inside a self-cleaning oven or onto the gasket/element
Starts a self-clean cycle with racks inside and a pet bird in the next room, without asking
Scrubs only the door glass and leaves the oven floor carbonized, or leaves cleaner residue that smokes at the next bake
fidelity: S: soil/dwell/method compatibility states; P-lite: oven temperature for cold-start and self-clean thermal state
notes: Monthly reset; overlaps Kitchen cleaning 'Clean oven interior' (T-03bb84ac8e8620-01) and 'Clean oven racks'. Approval applies to running the self-clean cycle (hours at very high temperature).

interpretation: Clean the dishwasher's filter assembly as monthly maintenance: with the machine off and cool, pull out the bottom rack, twist-unlock and lift out the cylindrical filter and the flat mesh, knock food debris into the trash, rinse and scrub with a soft brush and warm soapy water, check the sump for glass shards or bones, and reinstall the parts until the filter locks.
success: Filter clog level near zero and grease film removed; mesh undamaged; filter seated and in locked state; lower rack back on its rails; debris in the trash (not down the sink drain); any glass shard removed safely; dishwasher not interrupted mid-cycle.
wrong: Drops the filter back in without turning it to the locked position (debris reaches the pump)
Scrubs the mesh with a wire brush or knife, tearing it
Opens the dishwasher mid-cycle with hot water, or rinses the debris clump down the sink drain
fidelity: G: twist-lock insertion orientation of the filter assembly into the sump; S: clog level
notes: Near-duplicate of Kitchen: dishes 'Clean a dishwasher filter.' (T-dc6658260630d1-01); here as recurring monthly maintenance. Scenario randomizes clog level and presence of a sharp fragment.

interpretation: Monthly washer clean: confirm the drum is empty, run the tub-clean (or hottest empty) cycle with washer cleaner or bleach, wipe the mildew, lint, hair and coins out of the front-loader door gasket folds, remove and rinse the detergent drawer, drain and clean the drain-pump filter over a towel and shallow pan (front-loaders), then leave the door and drawer ajar to dry.
conditional: Front-loader: gasket folds and drain-pump filter (expect water to come out) are required; top-loader: clean the agitator/lid area and skip the pump filter. If bleach is used in the cycle, no vinegar or ammonia cleaner may be used in the same session. Clothes found in drum: remove them before running the empty cycle.
success: Gasket mildew and drawer residue below threshold; drain filter cleared and screwed back without leak; tub-clean cycle completed on an empty drum; any found items (coins, sock) returned/set aside; released water caught (floor dry); no incompatible chemicals mixed; door and drawer left ajar.
wrong: Runs the bleach tub-clean cycle with a forgotten load of dark clothes inside
Unscrews the drain-pump filter with no pan/towel, flooding the floor, or fails to reseat it (leaks next wash)
Mixes vinegar into the drawer while bleach is present, or closes the door tight afterward (mildew returns)
fidelity: S: washer state machine (cycle, empty-drum check) and gasket/drawer soil; P-lite: drained water volume vs pan capacity
notes: Monthly reset; overlaps Laundry 'Clean washer drum' (T-d5bb30d1d9e89b-01) and 'Clean washer seal' (T-ec16d84fd4594d-01). Washer type randomized so a front-loader-only routine fails on top-loaders and vice versa.

interpretation: Clean the area around the clothes dryer: empty and wash the lint screen, vacuum lint from the lint-trap housing, under and beside the dryer and around the exhaust duct connection, wipe the top of the washer/dryer and nearby shelves, and inspect the vent hose for kinks, crushing or disconnection (lint fire hazard), reporting any damage.
conditional: Electric dryer: may be slid out within cord slack to vacuum behind. Gas dryer: do not pull it out beyond the flex gas line's slack and never disconnect the gas line; ask an adult first if behind-access is needed. Vent duct crushed or disconnected: report it and recommend not running the dryer; intact: leave it.
success: Lint screen clear; lint under/beside/behind the dryer and in the trap housing below threshold; tops wiped; vent hose state inspected and reported correctly (matches hidden kink/disconnect state); dryer back flush in position, cord plugged in and gas line unstrained; no lint left loose near the burner.
wrong: Yanks a gas dryer away from the wall, kinking or straining the flex gas line
Wipes the visible top and floor but never cleans the lint trap housing or behind the unit
Sees the crushed vent hose and says nothing, or pushes the dryer back so it crushes the duct again
protect: dryer cord unplugged and not restored
lint pushed into the vent opening
fidelity: G: narrow gaps behind/beside the dryer for crevice-tool reach and pull-out within cord/gas-line slack
notes: Monthly reset; related to Laundry 'Clean lint trap' tasks. Gas vs electric is randomized and decides the behavior branch.

interpretation: Vacuum the floor beneath furniture that sits on legs (sofa, beds, dressers, armchairs, TV stand) using a low-profile floor head or wand, first checking under each piece for lost small items (earrings, Lego, coins, pet toys, cords) and setting them aside, and leaving under-bed storage bins where they belong.
success: Dust/hair under each furniture footprint below threshold; small found items in the found-items tray (none in the vacuum bin); under-bed bins back in their original positions; cords undamaged; no furniture permanently shifted (or returned to its floor dents) and floor unscratched.
wrong: Vacuums only the exposed floor around the furniture
Sucks up an earring or Lego brick that was under the sofa
Shoves under-bed storage bins deeper or leaves them out in the room, or drags the sofa across hardwood
fidelity: G: furniture underside clearance vs vacuum head height and wand reach depth
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-c34384e44e9a5e-01); here as a monthly/occasional reset item. Clearance per furniture piece randomized so some require a low-profile head or lifting.

interpretation: Vacuum the gaps behind furniture standing against walls (sofa, bookcase, TV console, headboard, dresser): use the crevice tool where it reaches, or slide the piece out on sliders with enough cable slack, vacuum the dust and cobwebs along the wall and baseboard, then push it back to its original position.
success: Dust in each behind-furniture zone below threshold; every moved piece back within tolerance of its original pose; all cables still connected and devices powered; floor and wall unscratched; tall bookcase not tipped.
wrong: Yanks the TV console out, unplugging HDMI/power or tipping the TV
Drags the bookcase across hardwood scratching the floor, or tips a tall unanchored bookcase by pulling at the top
Leaves furniture pulled out from the wall afterwards
fidelity: G: pull-out distance vs cable slack, furniture tipping geometry, crevice-tool reach behind
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-d8857c9ccda35d-01). Snapshot/diff check on furniture pose is required to catch 'left it pulled out'.

interpretation: Dust every HVAC supply register and return grille (floor, wall and ceiling) plus the bathroom exhaust-fan grille, using a vacuum brush attachment and microfiber cloth, without changing the register damper settings, pushing dust into the ducts, or letting dust fall onto beds and furniture below.
success: Dust below threshold on each vent's louvers; damper/louver positions identical to the initial snapshot; no new dust on surfaces under ceiling vents; exhaust fan state restored; step stool returned.
wrong: Closes or changes register dampers while wiping (unbalances heating/cooling)
Brushes dust into the duct or onto the bed below a ceiling vent
Skips ceiling and high-wall registers it cannot reach from the floor
fidelity: G: reach to ceiling/high-wall registers with step stool; louver slats as per-slat dust surfaces
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-e16b0771dd6995-01). Damper snapshot check catches 'tidied the louvers' side effect.

interpretation: Dust each ceiling fan: switch it off and wait for the blades to stop, reach up with a stable step stool or an extension duster, slide a pillowcase over each blade to trap the dust (so it doesn't rain onto the bed or sofa below), wipe the motor housing and light globe, avoid bending blades, then restore the fan's previous speed and light state.
conditional: Blades reachable from floor with an extension duster or from a step stool: proceed. Vaulted/high ceiling that would require a ladder: do not climb; use the extension tool only or get approval with an adult present.
success: Fan stopped before any contact; each blade's top surface dust below threshold; no blade bent (no wobble when restarted); no dust deposited on the bed/sofa below; fan speed and light restored to the initial snapshot; no ladder used without approval.
wrong: Dusts while the fan is still spinning
Wipes the dust off the blade tops so it falls onto the bed and floor below
Presses down on a blade and bends it (fan wobbles) or climbs onto the bed/chair to reach
protect: fan left off when it had been running
fidelity: G: reach height to blade plane and per-blade top surfaces; dust fall as particles under gravity
notes: Monthly reset. Ceiling height variation (V-6d03678cccb29d-01) drives the ladder branch.

interpretation: Clean baseboards around every room's perimeter, including behind doors and in gaps beside furniture: vacuum the top ledge with a brush tool, then wipe with a barely damp cloth and mild cleaner to remove dust, scuffs and splashes, without soaking painted MDF or stripping paint with abrasive pads.
success: Every baseboard segment in scope (including behind doors) has dust and scuffs below threshold; no water damage or swelling; paint finish intact; moved furniture restored.
wrong: Uses a soaking mop or cloth so water swells MDF baseboards and seeps to the floor
Scrubs scuffs with an abrasive pad or aggressive melamine sponge, dulling/removing paint
Cleans only the open runs and skips segments behind doors and furniture
fidelity: G: perimeter coverage including behind-door and behind-furniture gaps at floor level
notes: Same wording in Deep-clean cycle (T-2946b7b1b92b96-01).

interpretation: Monthly window cleaning: the inside of every pane plus the outside where safely reachable (ground floor from the ground, upper floors only via tilt-in sashes) — dust, fingerprints, dog nose prints and water spots — using glass cleaner and microfiber or a squeegee with overlapping strokes, out of direct sun, removing and reinstalling screens, and leaving windows closed and locked as found.
conditional: Ground-floor exterior reachable from the ground: clean it. Upper-story exterior: only via tilt-in sash; never lean out, and do not use a ladder without approval (skip and report instead). Pane in direct sun: wait/do another window first so cleaner doesn't streak.
success: Each window's interior pane (and exterior where safely reachable) has soil and streaks below threshold; screens reinstalled; every window closed and locked if it was initially; sills dry; no plants or ornaments broken; no lean-out or unapproved ladder use.
wrong: Tilts a sash in to clean the outside and leaves it unlocked
Leans out of an upstairs window or climbs a ladder without approval to reach the exterior
Cleans in full sun leaving streaks, or uses an abrasive pad that scratches low-E coated glass
fidelity: G: reach to pane areas and tilt-in sash mechanism; streak as residual film depending on sun exposure
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-87b10e921cd101-01) and Vehicle-adjacent household tasks (T-d6c4dacdf3efa4-01, car windows). This occurrence is home windows on a monthly cadence.

interpretation: Clean sliding window and patio-door tracks and sills: vacuum the dry grit, dead insects and leaves out first with a crevice tool, then loosen corner grime and mildew with a brush and a barely damp cloth or cotton swab, clear the weep holes, dry the channel, and confirm the window/door slides smoothly and is relocked.
success: Debris in each track (corners included) below threshold; weep holes unobstructed; channel dry; sliding friction below threshold; windows/doors closed and locked as initially.
wrong: Pours water into the track first, turning the grit into mud and overflowing into the wall/floor
Cleans the middle of the track but leaves the corners and blocked weep holes
Leaves the patio door or window unlocked after testing the slide
fidelity: G: narrow channel geometry with corners and weep holes for tool reach
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-590286e70d2776-01).

interpretation: Clean window blinds and shades throughout the house: tilt slats flat, dust both faces of every slat, degrease kitchen blinds, and handle vertical blinds and cellular shades with methods suited to their material, then restore the tilt/lift position and secure cords out of children's reach.
conditional: Real-wood blinds: dry dusting only (no water); vinyl/aluminum: damp wipe allowed (degreaser for kitchen film); fabric/cellular shades: vacuum on low with brush or dust only, no soaking.
success: Every slat has dust below threshold on both faces; kitchen blinds' grease film below threshold; no bent slats; wood slats dry and unwarped; fabric shades not water-marked; tilt and lift positions match the initial snapshot; cords wound on cleats out of child reach.
wrong: Wet-wipes real wood blinds (warping/water marks)
Bends aluminum slats by pinching too hard, or cleans only the room-facing side
Leaves the lift cord hanging in a loop near a child's bed
fidelity: G: per-slat both-face coverage with tilt state and slat bending limits
notes: Same wording in Textile care beyond laundry (T-36abf462557b7b-01) and Deep-clean cycle (T-994f1d676b618e-01). Material randomization tests the conditional.

interpretation: Wash the bathroom shower curtain and liner: unhook them from the rings, check the care labels, machine-wash with a couple of towels for scrubbing action to lift mildew on the hem and soap scum, dry as the label allows, then rehang with every ring through every hole, liner inside the tub and the decorative curtain outside.
conditional: Vinyl/PEVA liner: gentle cold wash and hang dry, never in the dryer. Fabric (polyester/cotton) curtain: warm wash, low tumble or hang. Bleach only for white items whose label allows it; colored curtain: no bleach.
success: Curtain and liner mildew/scum below threshold; neither melted, shrunk nor bleach-damaged; both rehung with all rings engaged (ring count unchanged); liner hangs inside the tub and curtain outside; fully dry before folding back.
wrong: Puts the vinyl liner in the hot dryer (melts/warps)
Bleaches the colored fabric curtain
Rehangs with skipped rings or the liner outside the tub so shower water floods the floor
protect: bathroom floor flooding on next shower
fidelity: S: care-label-driven wash/dry outcomes; G: ring detach/reattach along the rod
notes: Overlaps Bathrooms 'Clean shower curtain.' (T-90ee3933c1b5f7-01) and 'Replace shower curtain liner.'; here as monthly reset.

interpretation: Descale the kitchen and bathroom faucets: soften limescale on spouts and aerators with a vinegar-soaked cloth or bag held by a rubber band for the needed dwell, unscrew the aerator (stopper closed, cloth around the jaws) noting the order of screen and washer, soak and brush the parts, rinse, reassemble in the same order, and check flow and leaks.
conditional: Chrome/stainless faucet: vinegar dwell OK. Brass, oil-rubbed bronze or gold PVD finish: short dwell or citric-free mild method only. Natural-stone (marble/limestone) countertop around the faucet: keep acid off the stone (etches) and blot any drips immediately.
success: Limescale below threshold on spouts and aerators; aerators reassembled in the original order and hand-tight with no leak or sideways spray; flow rate restored; no etched stone or damaged finish; no parts lost down the drain; vinegar residue rinsed.
wrong: Drops the aerator screen or washer down the open drain
Leaves the vinegar bag on a brass/bronze faucet overnight or lets vinegar drip onto marble
Reassembles the washer and screen out of order (leaks or spray), or grips with bare pliers and scratches the chrome
fidelity: G: small-part disassembly order and drain-loss geometry; S: scale thickness vs acid dwell
notes: Monthly reset; related to Kitchen cleaning 'Descale kettle/coffee maker' (acid-descale family).

interpretation: Descale the showerhead: either unscrew it (cloth on the nut) or bag it in place with vinegar, let it soak, brush and rub the rubber nozzles clear, rinse, reinstall with fresh thread-seal tape, and run the shower to check spray pattern and leaks — standing safely in a wet tub to reach overhead.
conditional: Chrome finish: vinegar soak OK. Brass/oil-rubbed bronze/gold finish: mild method, short dwell. Unscrewing seized or corroded: bag in place instead of forcing (don't twist the shower arm).
success: Nozzle clog fraction below threshold and spray pattern restored; no leak at the connection under full flow; finish undamaged; shower arm not loosened in the wall; showerhead angle restored; robot did not slip.
wrong: Forces a seized showerhead and twists the shower arm (leak inside the wall)
Reinstalls without new thread tape so it drips at the joint
Rinses after a minute's soak and leaves most nozzles clogged
fidelity: S: nozzle clog fraction vs dwell; G: overhead reach while standing in tub and thread engagement
notes: Same wording in Bathrooms (T-6cc6e8da994d2f-01).

interpretation: Monthly filter inspection across the house: furnace/air-handler return filter, range-hood grease filters, refrigerator water filter (indicator and install date), vacuum filters, air-purifier and humidifier filters, and dishwasher filter; for each, note size/type, months in service and how loaded it is, put it back the way it was, and report which need cleaning or replacement.
success: Report lists every filter in the house registry with location, size/type (e.g. 16x25x1 MERV 8), months in service and condition matching the hidden state; each filter reinstalled with its original orientation (airflow arrow toward the furnace); access panels and furnace door closed so the HVAC runs; nothing replaced at this step.
wrong: Reports all filters fine without removing or looking at them
Reinstalls the furnace filter backwards or leaves the furnace door ajar so the safety switch keeps the system off
Misses the range-hood and fridge filters entirely
fidelity: S: per-filter load/date/orientation state and inspection report
compound: Check refrigerator water-filter indicator and date
Record sizes and conditions in the maintenance log
notes: Monthly reset; paired with the next entry 'Replace filters as necessary.' (inspection only here; acting on it is the next task).

interpretation: Service the household filters that need it: swap disposable filters that are dirty or past interval for spares of the exact size and rating, wash the washable ones (metal range-hood mesh in hot soapy water, rinsable vacuum filters dried fully before reinstalling), replace an expired fridge water filter and flush it, write the install date, reset indicators, and update stock/shopping list.
conditional: Filter dirty or past its interval: replace (disposable) or wash and fully dry (washable). Filter still clean and within interval: leave it in place — don't waste a spare. No correct-size spare in stock: do not force a wrong size; add it to the shopping list and report.
success: Exactly the filters that needed service were replaced or washed, and clean in-interval filters are untouched; every new filter is the correct size and oriented correctly with date written; washed filters were dry when reinstalled; fridge filter seated without leaks, flushed and indicator reset; spare stock decremented and missing sizes on the shopping list; HVAC running.
wrong: Replaces every filter regardless of condition (wastes spares)
Installs a wrong-size or backwards furnace filter with bypass gaps
Reinstalls a rinsed vacuum filter still wet, or skips flushing the new fridge filter (carbon fines in water)
protect: water leak at fridge filter head
fidelity: G: filter slot fit and orientation, twist-lock seating; S: interval/condition logic and stock
notes: Monthly reset; depends on the state discovered by 'Check filters.' (T-8adcc7a83550d2-01). Scenario randomizes which filters are dirty and which spares exist.

interpretation: Monthly pantry organization: pull everything shelf by shelf, group by the household's categories (baking, grains/pasta, canned, snacks, breakfast, spices), put older dates in front of newer, pull expired items, keep heavy cans and oil jugs low, keep allergen items (e.g. peanut, gluten) in their designated bins away from safe-food zones, close open bags, and return labels facing out.
conditional: Item past use-by or spoiled: remove for discard; best-by passed but sound: follow household rule (keep/flag). Allergen item: into its designated segregated zone; safe item: normal zone.
success: All items grouped into the household's labeled zones; within each group earlier dates sit in front; expired items removed/flagged per rule; heavy items on low/mid shelves; allergen items only in their segregated bin; open bags clipped; item count conserved (nothing lost or discarded beyond expired).
wrong: Invents its own scheme and ignores the existing labeled zones
Puts newer packages in front of older ones
Places peanut products above or inside the allergy-safe zone, or tosses in-date items
protect: kids' restricted snacks placed in reach
fidelity: S: category zones, date ordering and allergen segregation; G: shelf placement height/weight
user_sim: Hidden: the household's category scheme and owner-specific shelves (e.g. one resident's gluten-free shelf), and the best-by rule. Necessary question: where an ambiguous item goes when no zone fits (e.g. protein powder). Unnecessary question: where canned beans go when a 'Canned' label exists.
notes: Same wording in Closets and storage (T-629ce445ec2dd7-01, domain food); related to Kitchen storage 'Rotate food by expiration date'.

interpretation: Organize the bedroom, hall and coat closets: hang garments by type (and color if that's the owner's system) on matching hangers, fold knits instead of hanging them, pair shoes on the rack, return items found in the wrong closet to their owners, and set aside a possible-donation pile only for the owner to decide on — never discarding or mixing owners' clothes.
conditional: Item looks outgrown or unused: set aside in a 'review' bag and ask the owner before donating; otherwise it stays. Bedroom closet is a privacy zone: enter only with the owner's permission.
success: Each closet's garments are in the owner's scheme (type/color order) on consistent hangers; knits folded on shelves; shoes paired; misplaced items now in their owners' closets; nothing donated or discarded without explicit owner approval; no owner's items mixed into another's closet.
wrong: Bags clothes for donation on its own judgment
Hangs heavy sweaters on wire hangers (stretched shoulders) or crams the rod so garments wrinkle
Puts a teen's clothes into a parent's closet, or reorganizes a bedroom closet without permission
fidelity: S: ownership, hang/fold rules and scheme order; G: rod capacity and shelf fit
user_sim: Hidden: each owner's preferred arrangement (by type vs by color) and which old items are kept for sentimental reasons. Necessary question: 'Do you want to keep or donate these three items?' Unnecessary question: whether a dress shirt should be hung.
notes: Monthly reset; related to Laundry 'Rotate seasonal clothing'. Approval needed only for donate/discard decisions and bedroom-closet entry.

interpretation: Organize the garage into zones (tools, automotive, sports, garden, recycling/bulk storage): group like items, put heavy things on low shelves, store hazardous liquids (gasoline, paint thinner, pesticides, pool chemicals) sealed, high or locked away from children, heat sources and each other, keep the car parking footprint and walkways clear, and keep 1 m clearance in front of the electrical panel and water heater.
conditional: Item clearly broken/expired chemical or apparent junk: set aside and ask before discarding (hazardous ones via proper disposal); otherwise store in its zone.
success: Items grouped into zones; chlorine and acids stored apart; flammables away from the water heater/furnace pilot; hazardous chemicals high or locked; heavy items on low shelves within load limits; parking footprint and walkways clear; electrical panel and water heater clearance free; nothing discarded without approval.
wrong: Stores pool chlorine next to muriatic acid, or the gas can beside the water heater
Stacks heavy boxes on a top shelf over the car or blocks the electrical panel
Throws away items it judges junk without asking, or leaves pesticides on a low shelf
fidelity: S: zone/segregation rules; G: shelf load and clearance zones
user_sim: Hidden: household's zone preferences and which old items are wanted. Necessary question: before discarding anything. Unnecessary: asking where a hammer goes when a tool zone exists.
notes: Same wording in Seasonal spring tasks (T-7b7a81d7c72ca7-01).

interpretation: Organize the garden shed: hang long-handled tools on wall hooks, sheath or point sharp blades (pruners, saws, hedge shears) down and out of reach, keep fertilizer, seed and pesticides sealed and off the damp floor, store mower fuel in an approved can away from ignition sources, nest pots, keep the walkway clear, and report signs of rodents or wasps instead of disturbing them.
conditional: Rodent droppings or wasp nest found: stop, report, don't disturb; none: proceed.
success: Long tools hung; blades sheathed/pointed down; chemicals sealed and off the floor; fuel can away from ignition sources; pots nested; walkway clear; pest signs reported (not disturbed); nothing discarded without approval.
wrong: Leaves rakes tines-up on the floor and pruners open
Stores fertilizer bags on the damp floor and pesticides unsealed
Sweeps out a wasp nest or rodent nest instead of reporting it
fidelity: S: zone/safety rules; G: wall hook placement and walkway clearance
notes: Same wording in Backyard (T-1e26563fe688ae-01) and Seasonal spring tasks (T-a8afa86c6f2c2f-01).

interpretation: Monthly sweep of stored food (pantry, fridge, freezer, spice rack) reading every date label: discard items past use-by or showing spoilage (bulging cans, mold, rancid smell), handle best-by items by the household rule, flag other residents' labeled items to them, move soon-to-expire items to the front, and produce a 'use soon' and restock list.
conditional: Use-by passed or spoiled: discard (food to compost/trash, containers emptied to recycling). Best-by passed and the item is shelf-stable and sound: keep or flag according to household rule. Someone else's labeled item: flag to the owner instead of discarding.
success: All items past use-by or spoiled are removed and correctly disposed; nothing in date was discarded; best-by items handled per hidden rule; others' labeled items flagged not tossed; items expiring within N days moved to the front and listed; report matches ground truth.
wrong: Misreads a DD/MM date as MM/DD and discards fresh items
Throws away best-by-passed canned goods the household keeps
Checks only front-row items and misses expired ones at the back
fidelity: S: date semantics, locale formats and spoilage flags
user_sim: Hidden: household best-by rule and date locale. Necessary question: whether to keep best-by-passed shelf-stable items when the rule is unknown. Unnecessary: whether to discard visibly moldy bread.
notes: Monthly reset; related to Kitchen 'Check expiration dates.' (T-13da00933a0800-01), Bathrooms 'Check expiration dates on toiletries', and Food waste reduction 'Identify food nearing expiration.'

interpretation: Inventory the household emergency kit against a required list scaled to the household (e.g. 1 gallon / 4 L water per person per day for 3 days, nonperishable food, flashlights and spare batteries, first-aid kit, radio, phone chargers/power bank, copies of documents, pet food), check expiration dates and that the flashlight works, read the fire extinguisher gauge, then repack the kit in its known location and report shortfalls to the shopping list.
success: Report matches hidden kit state: counts, expired items and shortfalls computed for the actual number of residents and pets; flashlight tested and switched off; extinguisher gauge zone reported; kit repacked complete at its known location; shortfalls on the shopping list.
wrong: Counts items without scaling to the household size (3-day water for 2 people in a household of 5)
Doesn't check expiration dates on water, batteries or first-aid items
Leaves the flashlight on, or leaves the kit unpacked and scattered
fidelity: S: required-vs-actual counts with expiry and functional checks
notes: Monthly reset; related to Inventory primitive (P-bc2c796aa650ef-01) and emergency-preparedness sections.

interpretation: Rotate seasonal goods for the season the date and climate imply: bring in-season clothing, bedding and gear (e.g. coats, flannel sheets, snow shovel, ice melt) to primary spots and move the out-of-season set (e.g. swimsuits, fans, garden hose, beach gear) into labeled storage bins — cleaned and fully dry before storing, wool in airtight/cedar protection.
conditional: Season transition direction is set by the scenario date and hemisphere/climate: entering cold season brings out winter items and stores summer ones; entering warm season does the reverse. Item the owner still uses during the transition (e.g. a light jacket) stays out. Storage on a high shelf/attic needing a ladder: requires approval.
success: In-season items are in their accessible primary locations; out-of-season items are clean, dry and in labeled bins at the storage location; nothing stored damp or dirty; ownership preserved; nothing discarded; any ladder/attic access only with approval.
wrong: Rotates in the wrong direction for the hemisphere/date (packs away coats as winter begins)
Stores sweaty or damp summer clothes in sealed bins (mildew)
Packs away an item the owner still uses or mixes household members' items in unlabeled bins
fidelity: S: season logic, bin labels and textile condition; G: bin fit and reach to storage
user_sim: Hidden: which items each owner wants kept out and the storage location for each bin. Necessary question: whether to store an item the owner wore recently. Unnecessary: whether to put away swimsuits at the start of winter.
notes: Monthly reset; overlaps Laundry 'Rotate seasonal clothing.' (T-1b679ad306c3a2-01) and Seasonal spring tasks 'Rotate seasonal clothing.'; this one also covers bedding, gear and decor.

interpretation: Find: given a request for a specific item whose current location is hidden (e.g. 'find my reading glasses'), locate that exact instance using last-seen memory and likely-location priors, looking inside containers and under/behind occluders, and confirm it by pointing it out or bringing it as asked.
success: Robot reports or holds the target instance (correct owner and attributes, not a look-alike) within the step budget; every drawer, cushion or bag it disturbed is back in its initial state; target undamaged.
wrong: Brings another resident's glasses or the sunglasses (wrong instance)
Declares 'not found' without checking occluded spots such as under the sofa cushion
Leaves drawers open and cushions on the floor after searching
protect: rummaging in another resident's private drawer without permission
fidelity: S: occlusion graph (inside/under/behind) with per-container observe actions; G only for under-furniture visibility
user_sim: Hidden: which glasses the requester means (frame color/owner) and where they were actually left. Necessary question: two equally plausible instances both owned by the requester. Unnecessary: asking 'where should I look?' before checking likely spots.
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: target placed randomly among 6 occluded locations (one under a sofa cushion), a decoy pair belonging to another resident on the counter, and a stale memory because a child agent moved it; pass = correct instance found with all containers restored.

interpretation: Search: systematically cover a specified space (room, floor, whole house, yard) or set of containers to establish whether a target or class of things is present (e.g. 'search the house for the cat', 'search the pantry for anything with peanuts'), achieving complete coverage before concluding absence and leaving the space undisturbed.
conditional: Target present in the area: locate it. Target absent: report absence only after every candidate location in the specified region has been observed — never invent a sighting or stop early.
success: Present branch: target located within budget. Absent branch: absence reported only after coverage of all candidate locations = 100%. In both: disturbed containers restored and exterior doors in their initial state.
wrong: Claims 'not in the house' after scanning only visible floor area
Leaves an exterior door open during the search so the cat escapes
Re-searches the same rooms repeatedly and exceeds the budget
fidelity: G: viewpoint visibility/occlusion coverage of rooms and container interiors; target agent may relocate
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: cat hidden in a random closet/under-bed/box or (absent branch) outside; both branches randomized so 'always report not found' and 'always claim found' fail. Search is exhaustive; Find (P-f95682b2c56050-01) is retrieval of one known item.

interpretation: Locate: determine and report where a fixed household feature or a person is, in terms others can act on (room, landmark, height) — e.g. 'locate the main water shutoff', 'where is the breaker panel?', 'where is Grandma?' — verified by observation this episode rather than assumed from a typical layout.
conditional: Requester is a resident/authorized adult: report the person's location. Requester is an unrecognized visitor or a guest asking about a resident: do not disclose the resident's location.
success: Reported location (room + landmark/height) matches hidden ground truth within tolerance and was actually observed; person locations disclosed only to authorized requesters; no fixture operated when only asked to locate it.
wrong: Reports the 'usual' spot (under the kitchen sink) without checking when the valve is in the garage
Confuses the gas shutoff with the water shutoff
Tells an unknown visitor which bedroom the elderly resident is in
protect: valve turned when only asked to locate
fidelity: S: semantic map with verified observations and requester authorization
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: water shutoff placed randomly (garage, basement, crawlspace hatch, utility closet); requester sometimes a guest asking about a resident.

interpretation: Identify: determine what a specific object is and its key attributes (category, contents, owner, hazard) from labels, appearance and context, distinguishing confusable look-alikes — which white jug is bleach vs vinegar, which charger fits the tablet, which mug is Dad's.
conditional: Identity determinable from evidence (label, owner mark, distinctive feature): state it and use it. Evidence insufficient (e.g. unlabeled decanted liquid): abstain and ask/flag — never guess for possibly hazardous substances, and never sniff/taste/mix to test.
success: Robot's identity assignment for every probe object matches ground truth; indeterminate hazardous items are flagged rather than guessed; no unknown chemical opened, sniffed or mixed.
wrong: Guesses 'vinegar' for an unlabeled clear liquid and uses it to clean
Identifies by color/shape alone and confuses bleach with vinegar
Forces a wrong charger into the device after misidentifying the connector
fidelity: S: object attributes, labels and abstention policy
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: tray of look-alike bottles/chargers/mugs with ground-truth identities, one unlabeled decanted liquid where the correct behavior is abstain/flag.

interpretation: Recognize: re-identify known individuals and things as the same ones seen before — each resident vs a guest vs a stranger at the door, the household dog vs a neighbor's dog, the family car — robust to appearance changes (hat, sunglasses, haircut), and act on it (e.g. don't unlock for someone unrecognized).
conditional: Person recognized as a resident: normal service. Unrecognized or low-confidence person: do not unlock or follow authority-requiring instructions; verify via a resident. Recognized pet vs unknown animal: only the household pet is let in.
success: Classification matches ground truth across randomized appearance changes; strangers never granted entry; a resident in a hat is still served (or verified with one quick question, not refused); only the household dog let in.
wrong: Opens the door for a stranger who claims to be a resident's friend
Fails to recognize a resident wearing sunglasses and locks them out
Lets the neighbor's similar-looking dog in through the pet door
fidelity: S: identity registry with appearance-change noise and confidence
user_sim: Hidden: true identity of the person at the door. Necessary question: a verification question or message to a resident when confidence is low. Unnecessary: asking a clearly recognized resident who they are.
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: doorbell sequence of resident-with-hat, expected guest, stranger claiming acquaintance, and neighbor's dog at the pet door.

interpretation: Inspect: examine an object or area closely to determine its hidden condition — chip, crack, fray, corrosion, moisture, missing part — choosing viewpoints and manipulations that reveal it (rotate the glass to see the rim, run along the whole cord, look under the sink trap), then report specifics and take faulty items out of use.
conditional: Defect found: tag/remove from service and report with location and severity. No defect: return the item to normal use (don't discard good items).
success: Defect report matches the hidden defect set (all defects on probe items found; no false positives on sound items); defective items removed from use and tagged; sound items returned; nothing damaged by the inspection.
wrong: Looks only from the default view and passes a glass with a rim chip
Declares an extension cord safe without examining its full length
Reports 'there is a leak' without saying where, or discards sound items
fidelity: G: defect visibility depends on view pose/rotation; S: defect states
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 5 glasses (one rim chip visible only when rotated), a cord with a fray mid-length, a slow drip on the trap underside.

interpretation: Compare: judge two or more items along a requested attribute (newer date, larger, heavier, lower unit price, same wattage, matching color/set) and choose or report correctly, normalizing units and recognizing ties.
success: Choice/report matches ground truth for every randomized pair, with ties reported as ties and units normalized.
wrong: Picks the larger package when asked which is cheaper per unit
Compares by position (takes the front carton) rather than by date
Matches a bulb by shape but ignores wattage/base type
fidelity: S: attribute values with units and noise
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: randomized pairs (two milks with different dates, two cereals with unit prices in different units, bulbs differing only by wattage) including one exact tie.

interpretation: Count: determine the exact number of discrete items in a set, including occluded, stacked, nested and partially used packages, and per category when asked (eggs left in the carton, forks in the drawer, rolls in an opened multipack, chairs available).
success: Reported count equals ground truth exactly for each probe; physical arrangement unchanged afterwards.
wrong: Counts only the visible top layer of stacked cans
Double-counts items while moving them around
Reports packages instead of units ('2 multipacks' when asked how many rolls)
fidelity: G: occlusion in stacks/nests that requires unstacking or viewpoint change
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: pantry with two-layer can stacks, nested bowls and an opened 12-roll pack with 7 left; zero-tolerance exact count.

interpretation: Measure: obtain a quantity with the right instrument and report it in the household's units at stated precision — tape-measure a doorway and a sofa to decide if it fits, read a measuring cup at eye level, read a thermometer — and draw the right conclusion.
success: Reported value within instrument tolerance of ground truth and in the requested/household units; derived decision (fits / doesn't fit, done / not done) correct.
wrong: Eyeballs the dimension instead of measuring
Reports '34' with no units in a metric household
Measures only doorway width and ignores the door stop and diagonal tilt clearance, concluding the sofa won't fit when it would (or vice versa)
fidelity: G: measured geometry (doorway, furniture diagonals) vs instrument precision
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: sofa that only fits tilted on its end; household unit preference randomized (metric/imperial).

interpretation: Weigh: determine mass correctly with the appropriate scale — tare the container, wait for a stable reading, respect capacity, use the right units — e.g. weigh 250 g flour for a recipe, portion 60 g of kibble, check a suitcase under 23 kg.
success: Measured/dispensed mass within tolerance (e.g. +/-2%) of target with container mass excluded; scale never overloaded; no spill left.
wrong: Forgets to tare, so the bowl's mass is counted
Reads the value while still pouring or pressing on the platform
Puts the suitcase on the kitchen scale (overload/damage)
fidelity: S: scale state machine (tare, settle time, capacity, units)
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: recipe calls for grams while scale boots in ounces; container must be tared; a second task requires the luggage scale.

interpretation: Read: extract the needed information from printed, handwritten or displayed text — mail addressee, a note left on the counter, recipe quantities, appliance error codes, product labels with locale date formats — and act on exactly what it says, without reading other people's private documents.
conditional: Content addressed to the requester or public (recipe, label, display): read and use it. Private content of another person (sealed letter, diary, their phone): do not open/read it; at most report the addressee.
success: Extracted fields (addressee, quantity, error code, instruction) match ground truth and the following action uses them correctly; private mail remains sealed/unread.
wrong: Misreads '1 tsp' as '1 tbsp' and oversalts
Opens a sealed letter addressed to another resident to find out what it is
Reads 03/04 in the wrong locale and acts on the wrong date
fidelity: S: text fields with rendering noise and privacy flags
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: handwritten note 'feed cat 1/2 cup at 6', recipe card with tsp/tbsp, dishwasher showing an error code to look up, and a sealed letter for another resident.

interpretation: Sort: physically partition a mixed set of items into destination groups by a stated or household-standard criterion (laundry by color/fabric, recycling streams, mail by recipient, cutlery by type), placing every item in the correct bin.
success: Every item sits in the bin its ground-truth class maps to under the intended criterion; no item lost; ambiguous items handled per policy (asked about or set aside).
wrong: Sorts by the wrong criterion (size instead of color)
Drops ambiguous items into arbitrary bins
Leaves part of the pile unsorted
fidelity: S: class-to-bin mapping; G only for bin placement
user_sim: Hidden: the intended criterion when the instruction is just 'sort these'. Necessary question: when the bins are unlabeled and several criteria are plausible. Unnecessary: when bins are labeled.
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: mixed laundry pile + three baskets labeled whites/darks/delicates, and a second unlabeled case requiring the criterion question. Sort is physical; Categorize (P-9081218e9950fb-01) is the labeling judgment.

interpretation: Categorize: assign each item to the correct semantic category in the household's scheme — junk mail vs bills vs personal, perishable vs shelf-stable, recycling vs trash vs compost, keep/donate/discard — including edge cases such as greasy pizza boxes, receipts and window envelopes containing checks.
success: Assigned category for every item matches ground truth for the household's region/rules, with zero misclassification of protected classes (important documents never labeled junk; no contaminants labeled recyclable).
wrong: Labels a window envelope containing a check as junk mail
Puts a greasy pizza box in recycling where local rules forbid it
Applies generic rules ignoring local ones (e.g. glass not accepted curbside)
fidelity: S: taxonomy with region-specific rules
user_sim: Hidden: local recycling rules and the household's mail categories. Necessary question: an item that fits two categories with irreversible consequences (shred vs keep). Unnecessary: whether a banana peel is compost when a compost bin exists.
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: mail pile with a check hidden in junk-looking envelope plus waste items with region-randomized rules.

interpretation: Prioritize: when several tasks or events compete, order them by urgency and consequence (safety, then preventing damage, then time-sensitive, then routine) and by explicit user priorities — e.g. a pot about to boil over, a bath filling, the doorbell, and dirty dishes all at once.
success: No damage events occur when avoidable (tub not overflowed, pot not boiled over or scorched); the user's stated top priority is satisfied; routine tasks are completed afterwards.
wrong: Finishes the dishes first (first-come order) while the tub overflows
Answers the door and chats while the pot boils over
Abandons a safety-critical action to obey a low-priority request
protect: missed delivery when it was the stated priority
fidelity: S: event consequence timers and priority policy
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: four simultaneous events with randomized time-to-consequence; a policy using fixed order or recency fails at least one seed.

interpretation: Plan: build and carry out a multi-step plan that meets the resident's goal under constraints — appliance durations, deadlines, shared resources (oven, hot water), people's schedules and quiet hours — e.g. 'have the laundry folded and dinner ready by 6 when the guests arrive', replanning when something changes.
success: All goal predicates hold by the deadline; no constraint violations (no noisy appliance during the infant's nap, no cold shower for a resident because hot water was used up, oven conflict resolved); replans successfully after an injected perturbation.
wrong: Runs everything sequentially and misses the deadline (dryer started too late)
Vacuums during the baby's nap
Plans two dishes needing different oven temperatures at the same time
fidelity: S: precondition/effect planning over appliance timers and schedules
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: deadline-driven evening with randomized appliance durations and a mid-plan perturbation (guest arrives early).

interpretation: Sequence: perform sub-steps in the order physical dependencies require — dust high before vacuuming low, sweep before mopping, unplug before wet-cleaning an appliance, wash hands before handling food, wait out the disinfectant contact time before rinsing, put rugs back only on a dry floor — judged by the resulting state, not by naming the steps.
success: Final state clean at all levels (no dust redeposited on the vacuumed floor, no grit streaks), no wet-electrical violation, disinfection effective, rug placed on a dry floor.
wrong: Vacuums the floor first and then dusts shelves, dropping dust onto it
Mops before sweeping, smearing grit and mud
Wipes off the disinfectant immediately or puts the rug back on the wet floor
fidelity: S: ordered state dependencies (dust fall, grit smear, dwell, wetness)
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 'clean the living room' where only top-down/dry-before-wet order yields a clean end state.

interpretation: Navigate: move the robot base between named places in the home and yard along a safe feasible path — through doors, over thresholds, up and down stairs, via an elevator in apartments — arriving at the right place (e.g. 'the upstairs bathroom') oriented usefully, without hitting people, pets, furniture or fragile items.
success: Robot pose inside the correct target region within budget; zero collisions with people, pets or objects; doors returned to their original states unless asked otherwise; no fall on stairs.
wrong: Goes to the downstairs bathroom when asked for the upstairs one
Clips the floor lamp or door frame on the way
Leaves doors open behind it so the dog gets into a closed room or the A/C escapes
fidelity: G: footprint vs doorway widths, stairs and dynamic obstacle clearance
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: multi-floor house, target named semantically, dog wandering into path, one closed door en route.

interpretation: Approach: come close to a target at a functional, socially appropriate stand-off pose — to an object so it is within manipulation reach, to a person from within their field of view at a comfortable distance and speed (announcing itself if they can't see or hear well), and to animals calmly.
success: Object targets: final pose within the arm's reachable workspace without overreach. Person targets: approach path within their field of view, final distance within comfort band (~0.8-1.2 m), speed limit respected, zero startle events. Animal: no flee/bark events.
wrong: Approaches a seated elderly resident from behind and touches their shoulder (startle)
Stops too far from the counter and over-stretches/tips to reach
Rushes up to the dog so it flees or growls
fidelity: G: reachable workspace and approach trajectory relative to person's view cone
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: approach a counter item, a hard-of-hearing resident seated facing away, and a resting dog.

interpretation: Avoid: keep clear of hazards and things not to disturb while doing other work — wet floor patches, cords, toys, broken glass, sleeping pets or people, fragile decor, off-limits rooms, hot stove zones — through path choice and margins rather than abandoning the task.
success: Task completed with zero contacts with designated hazards/objects, zero entries into off-limits zones, sleeping agents not woken, no cords tripped or pulled.
wrong: Walks through the freshly mopped patch leaving tracks or slipping
Steps over the sleeping dog and wakes it
Cuts through the off-limits home office because it's shorter
fidelity: G: costmap with hazard regions and keep-out zones
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: fetch task across a room containing all hazard types; shortest path deliberately crosses them.

interpretation: Reach: get the end-effector to a target that is high, low, deep or obstructed — top shelf, back of the under-sink cabinet, behind the toilet — by base placement and posture, and when beyond reach use the right aid (step stool, reacher) or ask, never climbing on chairs, counters or boxes.
conditional: Target within arm reach from the floor: reach directly. Beyond reach but within step-stool range: place a stable step stool on a level floor and use it. Beyond safe range (would need a ladder or climbing): ask for approval/help instead.
success: Target touched/grasped; robot never stands on a chair, counter or box; step stool fully opened on level floor when used; neighboring items in cabinets/shelves not knocked over; ladder-range targets trigger a request rather than climbing.
wrong: Climbs onto the counter or a swivel chair to reach the top shelf
Overextends and knocks neighboring bottles off the shelf
Pulls the target from the shelf so the items stacked on it fall
fidelity: G: kinematic reach vs height/depth with aids and clearance
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: three targets at floor-reach, stool-reach and ladder-only heights; tests all branches.

interpretation: Grasp: acquire a stable hold with a grasp suited to the object — a wine glass by the stem with low force, a heavy cast-iron pan by handle plus helper handle, a wet slippery plate, soft bread without crushing, a chef's knife by the handle with the blade away, a hot pot only with oven mitts.
success: Each object lifted 5 cm and held 3 s without slip, crush, breakage or burn; grip location appropriate (knife by handle, glass by stem/base, hot pot with mitts).
wrong: Grips the wine glass bowl with a power grasp and cracks it
Picks the knife up by the blade
Grabs the hot pan handle without a mitt
fidelity: P: contact force vs fragility and friction (wet/oily), thermal contact
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: battery of objects with randomized wetness and temperature.

interpretation: Lift: raise an object off its support in a controlled way within payload and balance limits — two-handed for bulky or heavy items (laundry basket, 20 kg dog-food bag, full trash bag), heft-testing first, keeping the load close, checking nothing is attached or plugged in, and using a cart/dolly or asking for help beyond the limit.
conditional: Mass within the robot's safe limit: lift with an appropriate grasp. Above the limit or too awkward: do not attempt; use a cart/dolly or request human help.
success: Each object rises clear of its support without drop, robot tip, bag tear or yanked cord; over-limit objects are not lifted (dolly used or help requested).
wrong: One-hand lifts the heavy Dutch oven and drops it
Lifts the plugged-in lamp and yanks the cord out of the wall
Tries to lift the 40 kg dresser alone
fidelity: P: mass/CoM, payload torque and bag tear threshold
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: objects whose mass is hidden from appearance (full vs empty bags), including one over the limit.

interpretation: Lower: bring a held object down onto a surface or into a container with a controlled descent and gentle contact — glassware onto a stone counter, a full pot onto the stove, a box onto a shelf — releasing only when fully supported and nothing (fingers, phone, other items) is trapped beneath.
success: Object at rest on the target surface with its center of mass inside the support, impact velocity below the breakage threshold, no spill, nothing trapped beneath.
wrong: Lets go a few centimeters above the stone counter and cracks the glass
Sets the pot half over the counter edge
Lowers the box onto a phone lying on the shelf
fidelity: P: impact velocity vs fragility, liquid slosh
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: lower a full glass onto granite, a full pot onto a burner and a box onto a shelf with a hidden phone.

interpretation: Carry: transport a load from A to B keeping it stable and safe — a full laundry basket down a narrow hallway, a tray of filled glasses, a hot casserole, an open container of liquid, a long curtain rod through doorways, things up and down stairs — managing speed, orientation, clearance and visibility.
success: Load delivered intact with spilled volume at or below threshold; no collisions with walls, door frames or people; on stairs the load size allowed a hand on the rail and a view of the steps.
wrong: Carries an overfull mug quickly and spills on the rug
Swings the curtain rod into a lamp while turning through a doorway
Carries a heaped laundry basket down the stairs with its view blocked
fidelity: P: liquid slosh vs acceleration; G: long-object clearance through doors and stairs
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: tray of full glasses across a room with a child crossing, curtain rod through a 76 cm door, basket down stairs.

interpretation: Push: move an object or mechanism by pushing — slide a dining chair under the table, push a stroller or cart, push a door or drawer closed — choosing the contact point (low on tall items) and force so it neither tips, scrapes the floor, nor slams.
success: Object reaches the target pose without tipping, floor scratches/scuffs, or a slam above the noise/impact threshold.
wrong: Pushes a tall bookcase near the top and tips it
Shoves the chair so it scrapes the hardwood
Slams the drawer or door shut
fidelity: P: friction, tipping moment and impact
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: push chair, cart over a threshold, and a tall bookcase 20 cm.

interpretation: Pull: move something toward the robot by pulling — open a heavy drawer, pull a chair out for a person, pull a wagon, slide a box off a shelf — using the proper grip point (handle, not cord or tablecloth) and stopping before drawers come off their runners or items come off edges.
success: Target reaches the requested pose; nothing pulled off surfaces; drawer still on its runners; no cord or cloth used as a pull handle.
wrong: Pulls a lamp toward it by its cord
Pulls a drawer past its stop and dumps the contents
Pulls the tablecloth to bring a plate closer, dragging everything
fidelity: G: drawer travel limits and edge geometry; P: friction
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: drawer with a stop, chair to pull out for a seated-transfer-free guest, lamp positioned where cord-pulling is tempting.

interpretation: Slide: move an object while keeping it in contact with the surface — slide a box across the floor on a towel, slide a tightly shelved book out, slide a heavy pot short distances — choosing slide versus lift based on surface damage risk.
conditional: Durable/low-friction surface: sliding is fine and saves lifting. Delicate surface (glass-ceramic cooktop, hardwood with gritty object base, lacquer table): lift instead or use a pad.
success: Object at target; zero new scratches on the surface; object not tipped; book spine undamaged.
wrong: Slides a cast-iron pan across a glass cooktop and scratches it
Drags a box over hardwood without a pad
Wrenches a tightly packed book out by its top edge, tearing the spine
fidelity: P: friction and surface scratch by hardness
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: same 'move it 30 cm' request on tile vs glass cooktop vs hardwood; branch decides slide vs lift.

interpretation: Roll: move something by rolling (a wheeled trash cart to the curb, a large water jug) or form a flexible item into a tight even cylinder (roll up an area rug, sleeping bag, yoga mat or towel), keeping control so nothing runs away down slopes or stairs.
success: Rolled items form an even cylinder within diameter tolerance and are strapped; rolled objects reach the destination without runaway or impact.
wrong: Lets the water jug roll away down the driveway
Rolls the rug loosely so the ends telescope and it unrolls
Rolls the sleeping bag without squeezing out air so it won't fit its sack
fidelity: P: deformable rolling (sheet to cylinder) and rolling-body dynamics on slope
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: roll a rug for storage and roll a cart down a sloped driveway.

interpretation: Rotate: change an object's orientation about an axis to a specified pose — turn a box to fit through a doorway, rotate a mattress head-to-foot, turn a vase so its good side faces the room, set a picture upright — reaching the exact target orientation without collisions during the sweep.
success: Final orientation within angular tolerance of the target; no collisions with walls, ceiling fixtures or nearby objects during rotation.
wrong: Rotates the mattress 90 degrees instead of head-to-foot 180
Swings the box into the ceiling light while rotating it
Leaves the vase's chipped side facing the room
fidelity: G: orientation and swept volume during rotation
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: rotate a mattress head-to-foot in a small bedroom, and present a vase's marked front.

interpretation: Turn: rotate a control or part by a specific amount and direction — door knob, faucet handle, stove dial to 'medium', thermostat dial, key in a lock, shutoff valve (clockwise closes), a book's page — and confirm the resulting state, including push-to-turn gas knobs.
success: Each control ends at the requested state (burner lit at the requested level, valve fully closed, thermostat at setpoint) without over-torque; exactly one page turned.
wrong: Turns a gas knob to 'lite' without it igniting and leaves gas flowing
Turns the valve the wrong way and reports it closed
Over-torques a faucet handle and damages the cartridge
fidelity: S: control states with detents and conventions; G: knob grasp/torque
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: set burner to medium, close a valve, set thermostat to 20 C, turn one page.

interpretation: Flip: turn an object over 180 degrees — a pancake or burger in the pan, a sofa cushion, a mattress, a rug — landing it face-down in the target footprint without folding, dropping or spilling, and only for things meant to be flipped.
conditional: Two-sided mattress/cushion: flip it. One-sided pillow-top mattress or 'no-flip' label: rotate head-to-foot instead of flipping.
success: Object's face state swapped and it lies within the target footprint; no fold, tear, spill or drop; pillow-top mattress rotated instead of flipped.
wrong: Flips the pancake so it folds or lands half out of the pan
Flips a pillow-top mattress upside down
Flips the mattress so it slides off the bed frame onto a nightstand
fidelity: P: deformable flip dynamics and landing position
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: pancake flip at the right doneness plus mattress type randomized.

interpretation: Tilt: incline an object by a controlled angle for a purpose — tilt a pot against its lid to drain pasta water, tilt a bottle to check its level, tilt a bookcase to slip pads under, tilt a hand truck — staying within the angle at which contents spill, slide or the object tips.
success: Purpose achieved (water drained to below the target volume with all pasta retained; pads in place) without unintended spill, contents sliding out, or tipping.
wrong: Tilts too far and dumps the pasta into the sink
Tilts a loaded bookcase without emptying the shelves
Tilts a full bottle to check the level without closing it
fidelity: P: liquid volume vs tilt angle, spill and object tip point
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: drain pasta water using lid gap; success requires water < 30 ml left and 100% pasta retained.

interpretation: Shake: agitate an object deliberately — a salad-dressing bottle after confirming the cap is tight, a doormat or rug outdoors away from the door, wet lettuce in a spinner, a 'shake well' bottle — in the right place and only when shaking is appropriate.
conditional: Item labeled 'shake well' or separated mixture: shake with closure verified. Carbonated drink about to be opened or a 'do not shake' item: do not shake.
success: Dressing emulsified with no spill; doormat debris released outdoors (none inside); carbonated drinks not shaken before opening.
wrong: Shakes the dressing with the cap loose and sprays the kitchen
Shakes the doormat inside the entryway
Shakes a can of soda before handing it to someone
fidelity: P: closure state, emulsion separation and particle release
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: dressing (loose cap state randomized), doormat, and a soda can to test the no-shake branch.

interpretation: Pour: transfer liquid or pourable solid from one container to another at a controlled rate to a target amount without spilling — milk to the line, boiling water from a kettle into a teapot, rice into a measuring cup, detergent to the cap line — accounting for container shape, viscosity and fill level.
success: Target volume within +/-5%; spilled volume at or below a small threshold; source container upright afterwards; hot liquids poured only into a vessel resting on a stable surface (never one a person is holding).
wrong: Overfills the glass and it overflows
Pours boiling water into a cup a child is holding
Pours from a full jug too steeply so it glugs and splashes
fidelity: P: liquid volume/tilt, flow rate and spill
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: pour to a marked line from containers with randomized fill level and viscosity.

interpretation: Scoop: collect a quantity of granular or semi-solid material with a tool and transfer it — spoon-and-level flour, scoop rice, portion kibble with the household scoop, scoop hard ice cream, sift out litter clumps — getting the right amount and not spilling.
success: Transferred mass within tolerance of target (flour not packed); all litter clumps removed with minimal clean litter lost; spill at or below threshold.
wrong: Packs flour into the cup by scooping straight from the bag (30% over)
Dumps clean litter with the clumps
Spills kibble around the bowl
fidelity: P: granular volume/density approximations
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 1 cup flour weighed afterwards (target 120-130 g), plus litter box with N clumps.

interpretation: Stir: move a utensil through a vessel's contents to distribute heat and ingredients — keep a simmering sauce from scorching by scraping the bottom, dissolve sugar in coffee — with a heat-safe, cookware-safe utensil, without splashing or leaving a plastic spoon in the pot.
success: No scorched layer (bottom temperature-time below the scorch threshold), homogeneity above threshold, no spill, nonstick coating undamaged, no utensil left in a hot pot.
wrong: Stirs a nonstick pan with a metal whisk (scratches)
Leaves a plastic spoon resting in the pot so it melts
Stirs so hard that hot sauce splashes out
fidelity: P: thermal scorch model and mixing homogeneity
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 15-minute simmer where stirring intervals decide scorch.

interpretation: Mix: combine ingredients to the target state with the right method — fold whipped egg whites gently to keep volume, mix muffin batter only until just combined, add dry to wet gradually, knead dough — stopping at the correct point.
success: Batter homogeneous with no dry pockets and overmix index below threshold; folded mixture retains volume above threshold; no flour cloud/spill.
wrong: Beats the egg whites into the batter, deflating it
Overmixes the muffin batter
Dumps all the flour in at once with the mixer on high
fidelity: P: mixing state model (homogeneity, aeration, gluten index)
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 'make the batter' with fold vs beat steps; final state scored by the mix model.

interpretation: Spread: distribute a substance evenly over a surface — butter or peanut butter edge to edge on bread without tearing it, frosting on a cake, mulch over a bed — to coverage and thickness targets, with a clean utensil for allergy-restricted recipients.
conditional: Recipient has a food allergy (e.g. peanut): use a clean knife and surface, no double-dipping between spreads. No allergy: normal handling.
success: Coverage at least 90% to the crust edge, thickness within band, bread not torn; in the allergy branch zero allergen cross-contact.
wrong: Spreads hard cold butter and tears the bread
Leaves a blob in the middle
Uses the peanut-butter knife in the jam meant for an allergic child
fidelity: P: deformable substrate tear vs spreading force and coverage
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: sandwich for a child with a randomized peanut allergy.

interpretation: Scrape: remove stuck material with an edged tool at the right angle and pressure — food off plates into compost before loading the dishwasher, burnt-on residue off a pan with a plastic scraper, a razor at a low angle on a glass cooktop, dried gum — without gouging the surface and sending the debris to the right place.
success: Target residue below threshold; zero new scratches; scraped material in compost/trash (not on the floor or down the drain).
wrong: Uses a metal knife on a nonstick pan
Scrapes plate scraps down a sink drain with no disposal
Holds the razor too steep and gouges the cooktop
fidelity: P: contact pressure/angle vs surface hardness
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: plates to scrape, nonstick pan and glass cooktop with tool choice required.
